CORRECTION: the board was on USB DATA ONLY in this window, NOT charging. (I had called it 'almost certainly charging' from its presence on USB alone; JD disputed it -- an ESP32 stays dark on that port with its switch off, and the board's screen showed no charging.) The two overlap at ~138-142; their mean is ~141. Both are below B1's 165-213. THREE TRIALS, curve method: T3 from 0 -> 120.4; T1 from 17.7 pm -> 132.3 (runtime 133.5); T2 from 50 pm -> 148.5 (runtime 136.4). K_CC rises with the starting level. Candidates: the charger's thermal limit (a linear charger dissipates more at a lower pack voltage), or the curve's shape below ~3.6 V. PLAN CHANGE: instead of charging at once, the board drains to the next RGB cut with a read a minute (bench_trial.py restarted at 00:26: --wait-cut --poll 60 --full). That gives trial 3 a runtime check under the same conditions as trial 2's (data-only USB, flash 2): if the runtime again reads ~7% below the curve, the gap is systematic (a load overhead or the curve), not trial 2's alone. The full charge (gate 8) follows the cut.

TRIAL 3 BY RUNTIME: unplug 23:25:03.99 -> cut ~03:41:59 = 4.2822 h; the level at the unplug by runtime = 19.78 x 4.2822 = 84.7 pm; K_CC = 84.7 / 0.6667 = 127.0 pm/h (126.8-127.3 for +-30 s). The curve said 80.4 at the unplug (K 120.4): the runtime reads 5.3% HIGH here, where in trial 2 it read 5.6% LOW (147.8 against 156.5). Both runs were on data-only USB on flash 2, so a USB load overhead would push both the same way. It did not: the gaps are the curve's local error (~+-5%, inside its +-5 pm), not an overhead. THE THREE TRIALS (mean of the two methods each): T3 from 0% 123.7, T1 from 1.8% 132.9, T2 from 5.0% 142.4; MEAN 133.0 pm/h, the value flash 2 already carries. K_CC rises with the starting level (~+18 pm/h per 5 points at the bottom), so a constant K_CC reads a little high in a charge from empty and a little low from higher up; the bench's charge-then-drain runs can map that later.

GATE 8: A REAL CHARGE FROM BELOW 50%, on flash 2, unattended on the relay from the RGB cut (night-run.csv; log-20261009-1308-full.csv, v5). RESULT: PASS. (1) chg LOST, OVERRUN, HANDOVER and SELF-CHECK are 0 in every one of the 56 ten-minute entries. (2) No rise past the evidence: below the clamp the model stayed far under the voltage's ceiling (03:54: level 2.0% against an estimate of 3600 mV under charge, ~6%; 04:54: 15.0% against 3888 mV, ~49%). The 5C reached the clamp at ~07:24-07:34. (3) The knee: VDD sat at 4211-4212 mV from 03:54 to 07:24, then rose (4215 at 07:34, 4225 at 07:44, +10 mV), climbing to 4382 by 12:54 as the charge current tapered. t_knee ~4.0 h from 0, where the model's knee falls (533 pm / 133 pm/h = 4.0 h, plus the 60 s qualification). This run does not support the worry that the charge stays at constant current past the VDD rise. (4) Termination: CHRG released between the reads at 12:48:50 (97.4%, charging) and 12:53:50 (100%, not charging). The charge took ~9 h 05-10 min from 0, and T_TAIL ~5.1 h from the knee (B1: 5.22). (5) The model's own 99% was due ~12:57, ~5 min after termination: no OVERRUN, and a FULL step of ~2.6 points (97.4 -> 100).
